subject: Materials Science
title: Ultra-High Molecular Weight Polyethylene
description: A 60-second lesson on Ultra-High Molecular Weight Polyethylene.

hook.text: A fiber lighter than water stops bullets better than steel. It sounds impossible.

buildup.text: UHMWPE fibers — brand name Dyneema — are polyethylene chains millions of units long.

discovery.text: Gel spinning aligns chains parallel, creating a fiber with the highest specific strength known.

twist.text: UHMWPE melts at just 150°C — it can't be used anywhere near heat, its fatal flaw.

climax.text: Climbing ropes, cut-resistant gloves, and naval armor all rely on this remarkable fiber.

punchline.text: The strongest fiber per gram is just really long plastic.

quiz.question: What is the main weakness of UHMWPE fibers?
options: They are too heavy for most applications
